# Lamentations 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Remember, YHWH, what has-happened to-us; look and-see our-disgrace!

**2** Our-inheritance has-been-turned over to strangers, our-houses to-foreigners.

**3** Orphans we-have-become, without-a-father; our-mothers [are] like-widows.

**4** Our-water for-money we-drink; our-wood comes at-a-price.

**5** Upon our-necks we-are-pursued; we-are-weary — no-rest is-given to-us.

**6** To-Egypt we-stretched-out [our]-hand, [and]-to-Assyria, to-be-satisfied [with]-bread.

**7** Our-fathers sinned — they-are-no-more, and-we bear their-iniquities.

**8** Slaves rule over-us; there-is-none delivering from-their-hand.

**9** With-our-lives we-bring our-bread, because-of the-sword-of the-wilderness.

**10** Our-skin like-an-oven burns, because-of the-burning-heat-of famine.

**11** Women in-Zion they-violated, virgins in-[the]-cities-of Judah.

**12** Princes by-their-hand were-hung; the-faces-of elders were-not-honored.

**13** Young-men carried the-millstone, and-boys stumbled under-[loads of]-wood.

**14** Elders from-the-gate have-ceased, young-men from-their-music.

**15** The-joy-of our-heart has-ceased; our-dancing has-turned to-mourning.

**16** The-crown has-fallen from-our-head; woe to-us, for we-have-sinned!

**17** For this our-heart has-become faint; for these our-eyes have-become dim —

**18** For Mount Zion which-is-desolate — foxes walk upon-it.

**19** You, YHWH, forever sit-enthroned; Your-throne [endures] from-generation to-generation.

**20** Why do-You-forget-us forever, forsake-us for-length-of days?

**21** Bring-us-back, YHWH, to-You and-we-will-return; renew our-days as-of-old —

**22** Unless You-have-utterly-rejected-us — You-are-exceedingly angry with-us.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **5:1**: Zekhor YHWH — 'Remember, YHWH.' The community prayer (not acrostic, unlike chs. 1-4) appeals to divine memory. To 'remember' in Hebrew means to act on behalf of.

- **5:19-22**: The theological tension: God's eternal reign (v.19) vs. apparent abandonment (v.20). The prayer for restoration (v.21) is followed by the book's devastating final question (v.22).

- **5:22**: Ki im-ma'os me'astanu — 'Unless You have utterly rejected us.' The book ends without resolution — an open wound. Jewish liturgical tradition repeats v.21 after v.22 so the book doesn't end on despair.

— EMET
